newsitem.title: UK: Licht sees world 1996/97 sugar output up 3.6 mln t.
newsitem.headline: Licht sees world 1996/97 sugar output up 3.6 mln t.

text.p: World sugar production should rise to 126.61 million tonnes raw value in the 1996/97 crop year, 3.55 million higher than in 1995/96, German statistician F.O. Licht said on Monday.

In its first estimate of 1996/97 production, Licht said the European Union (EU), would produce the largest amount of sugar in 1996/97, albeit as a collective producer, and turn out 16.86 million tonnes after a previous 17.01 million.
India was expected to follow close behind with an output of 16.75 million tonnes, down from the 17.83 million tonnes produced last year, Licht said.

"In spite of falling production in Eastern Europe and the problems encountered by the Indian sugar industry, world sugar production in 1996/97 is forecast to rise by 3.6 million tonnes this season," the Licht report said.
Licht said the fall in Indian production, while still exceeding domestic needs, would have no consequences whatsoever on India's trading position due to excessively high stocks.

The lower EU production was not sufficiently pronounced to have any material impact on exports and would be more than compensated for by an increase of 690,000 tonnes in non-EU west European nations, mainly in Turkey and Yugoslavia.
The cane sector, as usual, took the lion's share of the production estimate with 90.20 million tonnes of the 1996/97 total after the sector's previous output of 86.63 million.
"Production increases are expected in the main sugar exporting nations of Brazil, Thailand, South Africa and Australia which should greatly improve supplies of high quality raws," Licht said.
Brazil was expected to produce a record 15.02 million tonnes of sugar after 13.64 million tonnes.
Another harvest record was also expected from Thailand, where 1996/97 output was pegged at 6.75 million tonnes compared with last year's 6.38 million.
Bumper crops should also come from the world's other major cane producers, Licht said.
"South Africa has recovered from its four-year drought and is expecting a 46 percent increase in output to 2.6 million tonnes," it said. Production in 1995/96 totalled 1.79 million.
Australia would also notch up another record with 5.57 million tonnes after a previous 5.13 million.
Licht said Cuba would continue its output recovery this year and 4.80 million tonnes of cane sugar was expected after 4.53 million in 1995/96.
